newsitem.title: USA: Earthgrains sales up despite exchange rates.
newsitem.headline: Earthgrains sales up despite exchange rates.

text.p: Baked goods and dough products company Earthgrains Co said Monday its sales for the fourth quarter rose 5.4 percent to $387.6 million, despite the unfavorable impact of foreign exchange rates.

In the fourth quarter ended March 25, U.S. bakery products benefited from the December 1996 acquisition of Heiners Bakery in West Virginia, which bolstered sales in a typically slower season. This benefit was nearly offset by foreign exchange rates that impacted revenues from European operations, it added.

Earlier, it reported operating earnings for the fourth quarter, before a charge and tax credit, of $3.9 million or $0.39 a share. A year ago, it had a pro forma loss of $4.1 million or $0.40 a share, excluding charges.

"We are showing results from our fundamental strategy of linking with customers, improving cost-effectiveness, providing quality, value and variety to consumers, and taking advantage of industry consolidation," Barry Beracha, chairman, said in a statement.
